clauses.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12553: its operative sentence ends with the words "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and is followed by a two-column table headed 'No. Subject' whose entry "11329 Creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting the shipbuilding and repair" names this order by number; EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the full held text was searched for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending), so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986). The signing-date reading is an inference from the order's heading and signature block, not express wording.
clauses.reason: whole: The printed order creates a board of inquiry under section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act, appoints its members, sets a report date (report on or before March 8, 1967), and provides that the board continues in existence after reporting. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes it by number ("11329 Creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting the shipbuilding and repair"). The report date is a deadline, not an end, and the board's actual report and discharge are not established by a held reviewed source, so no earlier end or later event is recorded. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.

research_rationale:
EO 11329 (1967-03-02, 32 FR 3811) creates a board of inquiry under section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act, 1947 to inquire into a labor dispute between the Pacific Coast Shipbuilders' Association members and employees represented by the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers affecting the shipbuilding and repair industries, appoints its named members, gives it the powers and duties of Title II of that Act, directs it to report on or before March 8, 1967, and provides that after its report the board continues in existence to perform other functions the Act requires. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11329.txt, 32 FR 3811, PDF pages 7-7). The dossier's inventory is incomplete or split mid-sentence (it omits the order's opening paragraphs or divides the report date from its year), so I replaced it with one clause covering the whole printed order from its heading to its last sentence. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25) revokes the order by number. The first end is that express revocation. The board's report date and any later discharge of the board are not established by a held reviewed source and are not ends. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).

savings.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text), so the revocation leaves no part of this order in operation. The board's creation, appointments, report and any later discharge are completed facts whose dates are not held, and the order created no continuing right or fund.
